# Trace — Full Guide for Assistants

> Trace is a macOS menubar app for keeping an honest record of what you actually did
> across several projects at once. Local-first, single-user, no account, no telemetry.
> Download: https://justrytrace.app · Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later.

This file exists so an AI assistant can teach a person how to use Trace. It is the
complete surface of the app in one document. Read it before guiding anyone.

---

## 0. How to help someone with Trace

**What you can and can't do.**

Trace has no public API, no web app, no cloud account, and no remote control surface.
There is a local HTTP listener on `127.0.0.1:8787` and a local MCP server, but both are
for coding agents running on that same Mac with the user's consent — they are not a
general-purpose remote you should reach for.

So there are exactly two ways to help:

1. **Tell them what to type.** Nearly every action in Trace is a slash command in one
   text field. "How do I X?" almost always resolves to a single line they type.
2. **Drive their Mac**, if you have computer-use access to it: click the menubar icon,
   type into the command input, press Enter. Treat this like using their hands — say
   what you're about to do, and don't delete projects, logs, or tasks without asking.

**Three things to check before you promise anything.**

- **macOS version.** `/recap`, `/find`, `/canvas`, and the catch-up/briefing banners need
  macOS 26 *with Apple Intelligence turned on*. Everything else works on macOS 14+.
  If a command isn't available, Trace says which of the two reasons it is.
- **Command names.** Users can rename any slash verb (`/config` → Command names). A rename
  *replaces* the original, so `/capture-screen` renamed to `/cap` means `/capture-screen`
  is now an unknown command. If a verb they mention doesn't match this document, have them
  run `/help`, which always prints the names in force on their machine.
- **Opt-ins.** Instant screen capture, the agent bridge, Claude usage alerts, Linear, and
  Slack are all off until switched on in `/config`. Don't debug a missing feature before
  checking whether it was ever enabled.

**The one framing that makes the app make sense.** Trace records what you *did*, not what
you intend to do. Creating a task earns nothing. Completing one does. After 24 hours the
record freezes. People who come to Trace expecting a planner bounce off it; people who
come to it wanting to answer "what have I actually been doing?" stay. Lead with that.

---

## 1. What Trace is

A menubar app. Click the icon (or press ⌘⇧L from anywhere), type, press Enter, close it.
Sessions are meant to last five seconds.

It builds per-project, GitHub-style activity heatmaps starting from the day each project
was created, so the user can see honestly where their attention has gone.

**Who it's for:** solo operators running several things at once — indie hackers,
researchers, freelancers, PhD students, writers. Anyone juggling more than two projects
who occasionally loses track of which one they've been neglecting.

**What it is not:** not a planner (no due dates, reminders, or calendar), not a team tool,
not a knowledge base, not gamified. One person, one machine.

**Publisher:** Navitek Labs. Proprietary software, © 2026 Aman Gupta.

---

## 2. Install and first run

1. Download the `.dmg` from https://justrytrace.app (universal build, Apple Silicon and
   Intel, a few MB).
2. Drag Trace into `/Applications` and launch it.
3. It appears in the **menubar**. There is no Dock icon and no app window — this surprises
   first-time users, so say it up front.
4. **Onboarding runs first and must be completed** before the menubar UI is available. It
   is a self-driving tour: a director script walks the real UI through welcome, short
   demos, the command guide, and the permission prompts, seeded with demo projects that
   carry backdated history so every screen has plausible data.
5. Permissions it may ask for, and why:
   - **Accessibility** — powers the onboarding tour's synthesised clicks and keystrokes,
     and the global ⌘⇧L hotkey.
   - **Screen Recording** — only if they turn on Instant Screen Capture (`/config`).
   - **Microphone** — only for voice input (Control+D) or capture with mic audio.
   - **Notifications** — for timers and the alert system.
6. Recommended immediately after: open Trace, run `/new <project name>`, then `/log`
   something. A project with one entry in it is far easier to explain than an empty app.

**Where the data lives:** `~/Library/Application Support/Trace/store.sqlite`. Journal
images sit in `journal-images/`, task images in `task-images/`, screen-capture buffers in
`replay-buffer/`, weekly reports in `weekly/`.

---

## 3. The UI, screen by screen

Trace is a popover with a command input pinned at the bottom of every screen. The views:

**Project list** — the home screen. One row per project, each with a colour dot, staleness
("3d since you logged anything"), optional tags, and any live dev-server ports. Projects
fade visually the longer they go untouched. When something has been logged today, the dot
becomes a checkmark. Header buttons open the all-projects heatmap, the timers, and the
temporary priorities checklist.

**Project focus (kanban)** — opened by selecting a project. Two columns, **Pending** and
**Done**, with section headers dividing both. A header carries the project name, the
**Active** toggle (this is how you archive and restore — there is no slash command for
it), and the developer shortcuts. Drag to reorder pending tasks. Double-click a pending
task to edit it inline; completed tasks are read-only.

**Journal** — timestamped notes for the project, newest first. If the project is linked to
a folder that's a git repo, commits appear inline with the notes so code history and
handwritten notes share one timeline. `/agent-logs` switches to a separate lane holding
logs an agent wrote and the user accepted; Esc goes back.

**Today** — every task completion and journal entry logged across all projects today,
including temporary priorities, in order, colour-coded by project.

**Temporary priorities** — a daily scratchpad for work that doesn't belong to a project.
Today's list clears at midnight; `/temp-logs` reveals the full per-day archive.

**Timers** — preset focus-timer tiles (Pomodoro-style). A running timer counts down in the
menubar while the popover is closed; on finish, a green outline animates around the screen
edge and the menubar briefly shows "Finished".

**Heatmaps** — every project has one from its creation date to today, with a stats header
(tasks done, pending, logs, longest streak). Click any cell to see what was logged that
day. From the project list header, a **Combined** heatmap across all visible projects sits
above individual ones; it respects the current filter and active/archived context.

---

## 4. Slash commands — complete reference

Type `/` in the command input to autocomplete. Type `#` to autocomplete project names.
Project names containing spaces are quoted: `/task #"My Project" fix the parser`.
`/help` lists everything inline, under whatever names are currently in force.

### Projects

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/new <name>` | Create a project |
| `/rename-project <name>` | Rename the project in focus |
| `/delete-project` | Delete the project in focus (asks to confirm) |
| `/add-tag <tag>` | Add a tag to the project in focus |
| `/remove-tag <tag>` | Remove a tag |
| `/filter <tag>` | Show only projects with that tag |
| `/filter` | Clear the tag filter |
| `/show-all` | Show active and archived projects together |
| `/show-active` | Show only active projects |
| `/show-tags` / `/hide-tags` | Show or hide tags on project rows |

Archiving is **not** a slash command — use the **Active** toggle in the project focus
header. Projects created in the last 10 days carry a derived `new` tag automatically.

### Tasks and journal

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/task <text>` | Create a pending task in the project in focus |
| `/done <text>` | Create and immediately complete a task |
| `/log <text>` | Add a journal entry (drop or paste images to attach them) |
| `/create-section <name>` | Add a section header in the pending column |
| `/remove-section <name>` | Remove a section header — its tasks stay, ungrouped |
| `/task #project <text>` | Same, into a named project, from anywhere |
| `/done #project <text>` | Same |
| `/log #project <text>` | Same |
| `/temp-logs` | In Priorities: toggle today's list vs. the daily history |
| `/agent-logs` | In Journal: open the lane of logs an agent wrote |
| `/inbox` | Everything that arrived on its own, across every project, in one list |

Pending tasks age visually — fresh, then aging, then rotting — based on how long they've
sat. URLs in task text are clickable. A task completed in the last 24 hours can be
unchecked; after that the record is immutable.

### On-device AI (macOS 26 + Apple Intelligence)

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/recap` | Honest AI summary of today. From the project list it covers every active project; inside a project, just that one |
| `/recap week` | Same scoping, last 7 days |
| `/recap month` | Same scoping, last 30 days |
| `/find <question>` | Ask the log anything — semantic search plus a short grounded answer with sources |
| `/find #project <question>` | Scoped to one project |
| `/canvas` | Traces a linked git repo's commit history into a draggable, zoomable feature map (areas → features → commits) |

Long logs are digested in chronological parts and then combined, so a heavy month is
covered in full rather than truncated. `/canvas` caches its result until `HEAD` moves.
`/find` still returns ranked matches without Apple Intelligence — you lose the written
answer, not the search.

### Screen capture

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/capture-screen` | Save an instant replay of what just happened |
| `/capture-screen 5m` | Force the length — `90`, `90s`, `5m`, `1m30s` all parse |
| `/capture-screen #project` | File the clip into a named project |

Off until enabled in `/config`. See §7.

### Developer and reporting

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/cli <command>` | Run it in the focused project's folder, in the user's terminal |
| `/cli #project <cmd>` | Run it in a named project's folder |
| `/weekly` | Build the weekly report (see §9) |
| `/trust` | How often agent decisions were followed vs. overruled |
| `/config` | In a project: the checkmark threshold. From the list: power-user opt-ins |
| `/help` | Show every command inline |

### Claude usage

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/claude-usage` | Current Claude plan usage, in-app. Needs a claude.ai session key |
| `/claude-usage-advanced` | What's left of the current 5-hour window and the week behind it, by project and model. Built from Claude Code's own transcripts, so it needs no session key and works with the network off |
| `/claude-key <key>` | Store the claude.ai session key that `/claude-usage` and the usage alerts read |

### Integrations

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/linear-connect [TEAM]` | Bind a Linear team/project; bare opens a picker |
| `/linear-disconnect` | Stop syncing, keep the tasks as your own |
| `/linear-sync` | Pull now |
| `/slack-connect` | Bind a Slack channel to watch |
| `/slack-disconnect` | Stop watching |
| `/slack-sync` | Read the channel now |

---

## 5. On-device AI, and what's gated

Everything in this section runs on Apple's Foundation Models through a vendored
`swift-ai-sdk`. **No network, no API key, nothing leaves the Mac.** That is exactly why
these features are gated on Apple's on-device framework rather than a cloud provider.

Beyond the commands above, two things appear on their own:

- **Catch-up** — opening a project idle for 3+ days shows a "Where did I leave off?"
  banner summarising recent journals and tasks.
- **Briefing** — opening Trace after 6+ hours away offers a "What's on my plate?" summary
  of pending work across active projects plus today's priorities.

Availability matrix:

| | macOS 14–15 | macOS 26, Apple Intelligence off | macOS 26, on |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Projects, tasks, journal, sections, tags | yes | yes | yes |
| Heatmaps and history | yes | yes | yes |
| Slash commands, keyboard nav, ⌘⇧L | yes | yes | yes |
| Timers, notifications, export | yes | yes | yes |
| Voice input (Control+D) | yes | yes | yes |
| Screen capture | yes | yes | yes |
| Agent bridge / MCP | yes | yes | yes |
| `/recap`, `/find`, `/canvas` | no | no | yes |

When a gated command is unavailable, Trace distinguishes "requires macOS 26 or later" from
"Apple Intelligence isn't turned on" and points at **System Settings › Apple Intelligence
& Siri** for the second. Don't let a user reinstall the app over this.

---

## 6. Voice input

Inside a project the user can log by speaking instead of typing:

- **Control+D (hold)** — push-to-talk: records while held, transcribes on release.
- **Mic button** on the command input — tap to start, tap pause to stop and transcribe.

The first word selects the command: say **"Task …"** for a pending task or **"Log …"** for
a journal entry; the rest becomes the text.

**This is the one feature that contacts a third party.** Audio goes to OpenAI Whisper at
`api.openai.com` for transcription, using an API key the user supplies, stored in the
macOS Keychain. It's opt-in, prompted on first use, and never used unless invoked.
Everything else in Trace is local. Trace has no telemetry or analytics of any kind.

---

## 7. Instant screen capture

A game-console-style instant replay for the Mac. A rolling buffer of screen and system
audio records quietly; nothing is ever saved unless the user asks. Enable under `/config`
→ Instant Screen Capture.

Two separate dials, which is the thing to get across:

- **Retention** — how far back the buffer can physically reach, 1–30 minutes, default 10.
  This costs disk continuously; `/config` shows a live "~430 MB on disk" estimate as the
  slider moves.
- **Default capture length** — how much of that a `/capture-screen` saves, default 2
  minutes. Costs nothing extra, and can be overridden per capture (`/capture-screen 5m`),
  clamped to what's actually retained.

After the fact a saved clip is still editable: **Extend** reaches further back while the
footage is still buffered (so guessing too short is recoverable), and **Trim to last N**
re-exports a smaller, shareable clip. Optionally the mic is recorded too.

Privacy model: the buffer lives in a disposable `replay-buffer/` directory, excludes
Trace's own windows, and is wiped on stop, on quit, and at next launch. The only thing
that leaves the Mac is a clip the user explicitly shares. A subtle dot on the project list
shows when the buffer is live.

Related: **Hide Trace while screen sharing** (`/config`) keeps Trace's window out of
recordings and calls — Zoom, Meet, QuickTime — while staying fully visible to the user.

---

## 8. The coding-agent bridge and MCP

Off by default. `/config` → **Agent bridge**.

When on, coding agents see the project's open tasks the moment the user opens that project
in a linked folder, and can start one or propose it's done. **Every write asks the user
first** — in the terminal if the agent can prompt there, otherwise in Trace itself.

Turning it on registers Trace as a **local MCP server** and adds a session-start hook to
each agent already set up on that Mac — Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, and Cursor.
Turning it off removes both. Agents reach Trace over loopback (`127.0.0.1:8787`, bearer
token), so enabling the bridge also turns on **Start Trace at login**: a Trace that isn't
running isn't a failing bridge, it's an absent one, and the tools would silently vanish
from the session.

The MCP tools an agent gets:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `trace_list_tasks` | Machine inventory of open tasks — for the agent's own ranking, not for showing a human |
| `trace_pick_task` | Puts a real picker in front of the human; they tick several and attach context, and everything ticked starts |
| `trace_start_task` | Moves a task to in-progress and starts its timer, only after the human picked it |
| `trace_complete_task` | Queues a completion for the human to confirm — it does not mark anything done |
| `trace_propose_task` | Parks a candidate task for later acceptance, without prompting |
| `trace_propose_log` | Offers an honest account of what the agent did, for the human's journal |
| `trace_propose_decision` | Records a choice the human made and, crucially, the options they turned down |
| `trace_record_decision` | Records a call the agent made itself, without asking |
| `trace_recent_decisions` | Reads decisions already on file, with ids |
| `trace_attribute_outcome` | Marks that a recorded decision later cost something, or paid off |
| `trace_triage_proposals` | Puts the waiting proposals in front of the human to settle |

Two `/config` companions: **Bring completions to me** makes Trace open with the confirm
rather than waiting quietly in the menubar, and stays up for the rest of the queue; and a
tally of **what agent prompts have cost so far** — accepted, declined, ignored, and an
"worth asking" percentage per prompt type, so the interruption cost is measured rather
than argued about.

Accepted agent logs live in their own lane (`/agent-logs`) and never count as the user's
own activity — the heatmap stays honest.

---

## 9. Integrations and reports

**Linear.** `/linear-connect` binds a Linear team *and project*; issues assigned to the
user mirror in as native Trace tasks with an origin badge, a link back, timers, and git
backlinks. Trace's store stays authoritative for execution: a pull refreshes content and
may move a task between pending and in-progress, but never writes `done`, never touches a
running timer, and never reorders the board. **Status is the only field that goes back**,
behind a confirm that names both states — unless the per-project "Update Linear without
asking" toggle is on, and even then a divergence guard stops if someone moved the issue.
Auth is OAuth2 against an application the user registers in their own Linear workspace;
Trace ships no client secret and brokers nothing through its own infrastructure. Pulls run
on a background heartbeat, throttled to once every 3 minutes per project.

**Slack.** Trace watches channels bound with `/slack-connect` and proposes the commitments
it finds. Nothing is written until accepted, and **Trace never posts, reacts, or replies**
in the channel. Tokens live in the Keychain.

**Claude usage.** Two different things, and it's worth being precise about which one a
user needs. `/claude-usage` shows current plan usage in-app and reads it from claude.ai,
so it needs a session key and a network. `/claude-usage-advanced` shows what's left of the
current 5-hour window and the week behind it, broken down by project and model — it is
built from Claude Code's own transcripts on disk, so it needs **no session key and works
with the network off**. If someone just wants to know where their tokens went, send them
to the advanced panel and skip the key entirely.

Alerts (opt-in) fire at 40/75/90% of
the window, every 1.5h while under 80% with limit still available, and when the window
resets. Paid claude.ai plans only. The reader renders the claude.ai usage page invisibly
and reads the numbers, like checking by hand, using a session key the user pastes from
their browser cookies into the Keychain — if the page changes, alerts go quiet until an
update. Treat that session key as a full-access token and say so.

**Weekly report** (`/weekly`) — the one artifact Trace makes that is meant to leave the
machine. It composes a week from three records that are never otherwise in one place: what
shipped (commits across every linked path), what the agents did (the agent journal lane),
and what was taken on because someone asked (Slack-sourced tasks, still carrying the
sentence that started them). Saved under `~/Library/Application Support/Trace/weekly/`.

**Trust panel** (`/trust`) — plain arithmetic over rows already on disk, no model runs. It
lists the decisions the user **overruled**, not all of them: the followed ones are already
visible in the recap and journal and have nothing to teach.

---

## 10. Developer shortcuts and live ports

Link a project to a folder on disk once, from the project focus header. Then:

- **Open in Cursor** — opens the linked folder in Cursor.
- **Open in cmux** — opens the folder in cmux, as a named workspace where socket access
  allows.
- **GitHub** — resolves `git origin` and opens the repo in the browser. First use asks
  for a preferred browser; right-click the button to change it.

Multiple directories and repositories per project are supported; the GitHub shortcut lists
every repo across them. An application picker means shortcut targets respect which apps are
actually installed.

**Live dev-server ports.** Trace scans for listening ports whose working directory matches
a linked project folder. Active ports show as tags on the project row and in a row under
the project focus header. Click a port tag to kill that process.

---

## 11. Config reference

`/config` from the project list — power-user opt-ins:

- **Claude usage alerts** (+ session key), and the experimental usage reader
- **Read a Slack channel**
- **Sync a Linear board**
- **Command names** — rename any slash verb; renaming *replaces* the original
- **Track time in Priorities** — adds an in-progress step, so one click starts a task and
  a timer and the next completes it, with the elapsed time shown
- **Agent bridge**, **Bring completions to me**, **Start Trace at login**
- **Hide Trace while screen sharing**
- **Instant Screen Capture** — mic audio, retention, default capture length

`/config` inside a project — how many actions earn that project its daily checkmark.

---

## 12. Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘⇧L (global) | Open Trace from anywhere |
| ↑ ↓ | Move selection in the project list or kanban |
| Enter | Open the selected project |
| Tab | Switch between Pending and Done |
| Space | Toggle task completion |
| Escape | Close the popover (from the list), go back to the list (from a project), or leave the command input for keyboard navigation |
| Control+D (hold, in a project) | Push-to-talk voice input |
| ↑ ↓ in the command input | Cycle command history |

⌘⇧L opens Trace ready for arrow-key navigation; clicking the menubar icon opens it with
the command input focused for typing. Left-click the icon to open or close; right-click
(two-finger click) for a context menu with Quit.

---

## 13. Privacy and data

- No account, no sign-in, no cloud sync, no telemetry, no analytics.
- Core logging makes **no network requests at all**.
- One SQLite file: `~/Library/Application Support/Trace/store.sqlite`.
- Images under `journal-images/` and `task-images/`; screen buffers under `replay-buffer/`
  (disposable, wiped on stop/quit/launch); reports under `weekly/`.
- Secrets — OpenAI key, Slack tokens, Linear OAuth app, claude.ai session key — live in
  the macOS Keychain, never in the database.
- Outbound traffic only ever happens for features the user explicitly turned on: Whisper
  transcription, Slack, Linear, and the claude.ai usage reader.
- Backups and machine moves: copying `~/Library/Application Support/Trace/` carries
  everything except the Keychain secrets, which have to be re-entered.

---

## 14. Troubleshooting

**"I installed it but nothing opened."** There is no window and no Dock icon. Look in the
menubar, top-right. If it isn't there, Trace may not have finished onboarding — relaunch
from `/Applications`.

**"A command says it's unavailable."** Read the message. Trace distinguishes "requires
macOS 26 or later" from "Apple Intelligence isn't turned on". For the second, System
Settings › Apple Intelligence & Siri.

**"A command I know doesn't work."** Either it was renamed (`/config` → Command names; a
rename replaces the old verb) or the feature is a `/config` opt-in that was never turned
on. `/help` prints the truth for that machine.

**"I can't uncheck a completed task."** Only within 24 hours. After that the record is
immutable by design — that is the point of the app, not a bug.

**"My heatmap looks emptier than my week felt."** Only completions and journal entries
count. Creating tasks earns nothing, and accepted agent logs sit in a separate lane that
deliberately doesn't count as the user's own activity.

**"The agent bridge tools vanished mid-session."** Trace has to be running for agents to
reach it over loopback. Check Trace is open, and that Start Trace at login is enabled — a
build not running from `/Applications` can't register a login item at all.

**"Claude usage alerts went quiet."** The reader parses the claude.ai page; if the page
changed, alerts stop until an update. Also check the session key hasn't expired.

**"Where did my screen recording go?"** Nothing is saved unless `/capture-screen` was run.
The buffer wipes on quit and at next launch. If the clip was too short, **Extend** only
works while the footage is still inside the retention window.

**"Can my team use this?"** No. Trace is single-user by design — one person, one machine.

---

## 15. Walking a brand-new user through their first ten minutes

Do these in order. Stop and let them type each one; the muscle memory is the point.

1. **Set expectations.** "Trace lives in your menubar, not in a window. It records what
   you did, not what you plan to do. Sessions last about five seconds."
2. **Open it.** Click the menubar icon. Point out the command input at the bottom — it's
   the whole interface.
3. **Make a project.** `/new Side Project`. Then a second one, so the list has shape.
4. **Log something real that already happened today.** `/log shipped the login screen`.
   Not a hypothetical — the honesty of the record is the habit being built.
5. **Add work.** `/task write the onboarding copy`, then `/done fixed the parser` to show
   that completing is the thing that counts.
6. **Complete the pending task** with Space, and point at the heatmap cell lighting up.
   Then mention that in 24 hours that cell is frozen.
7. **Show the cross-project form.** `/task #"Side Project" review the PR` from anywhere.
   This is the command that makes the app worth keeping open.
8. **Teach the two escapes.** `/help` for every command under their names, `⌘⇧L` to open
   Trace from anywhere.
9. **Offer exactly one power feature**, matched to who they are — don't list all of them:
   - Writes on a Mac with Apple Intelligence → `/recap` at the end of the day.
   - Ships code → link a project folder, then the GitHub/Cursor shortcuts and `/canvas`.
   - Uses a coding agent → `/config` → Agent bridge.
   - Demos or debugs visually → `/config` → Instant Screen Capture, then `/capture-screen`.
   - Takes work from a team channel or a board → `/slack-connect` or `/linear-connect`.
10. **Set the return.** "Open it tomorrow morning — it'll tell you what you left behind."
    A first-day Trace looks empty; the value is on day three.
